note: The selected text follows the Benziger 1962 page letter for letter, with its accents, ligatures, capitals and punctuation. The separately set Vatican 1962 page, the 1952 Enchiridion and the 1961 Liber Usualis carry the same 149 words in the same order; the 1910 Raccolta agrees except for the case of the first word of the last strophe. The two Missal settings differ only in the spellings and punctuation positioned below. The Raccolta and the Liber Usualis print consonantal j, folded to i for comparison; the Enchiridion, the Raccolta and the Liber Usualis are compared for their letters only, because their accents, digraphs, capitals and punctuation follow their own conventions.

adjudicated.ruling: Retain súbiicit, as printed by the controlling Benziger page and spelled subiicit in the 1952 Enchiridion and subjicit or súbjicit in the 1910 Raccolta and the 1961 Liber Usualis. The Vatican setting prints súbicit, with a single i; both spell the same form of the verb subiicio (subicio).

Retain pǽnitens. with the æ of both 1962 Missal settings, matched by paenitens in the 1952 Enchiridion and paénitens in the 1961 Liber Usualis. The 1910 Raccolta prints pœnitens. with the œ spelling of the same participle.

Retain intúeor. with the full stop of the controlling Benziger page, which closes the first sentence of the strophe before Deum tamen. The Vatican setting prints intúeor, and runs the two clauses together; the words and their syntax are the same.

Retain pellicáne, with the double l of the controlling Benziger page, also printed pellicane by the 1952 Enchiridion and pellicáne by the 1961 Liber Usualis. The Vatican setting prints pelicáne, and the 1910 Raccolta pelicane, the single-l spelling of the same noun.
Retain lowercase sánguine, as printed by the controlling Benziger page and the 1961 Liber Usualis. The Vatican setting capitalizes Sánguine, as the 1952 Enchiridion also does; the word is the same.

Retain the vocative Iesu, printed by both 1962 Missal settings and the 1952 Enchiridion and as Jésu in the 1961 Liber Usualis, so that the strophe opens by addressing Jesus. The 1910 Raccolta prints the accusative Jesum, which puts the name in the case of the following relative quem as its antecedent instead of addressing him; this is a different grammatical reading, not a spelling.
Retain sítio: with the colon of the controlling Benziger page before the purpose clause Ut. The Vatican setting prints sítio; with a semicolon at the same point.
